fr.recommendations:
• Trim vegetation that is growing close to the detached structure to keep a clear path around it for responders working near that building.
• Cut back dense vegetation along any fenced sections to keep gate locations visible and reachable from the outside.
• Mark all gate locations with reflective signs or numbers so responders can find them quickly without searching along fence lines.
• Keep gates in fenced sections unlocked or secured with a lock box so responders can move between yard areas without delay.
• Clear a consistent walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without obstacles.
• Post the property address in large, reflective numbers at the driveway entrance so it is readable at night and from a moving vehicle.
• Identify the most direct route from the street to the front entry and keep that path clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and overgrown vegetation at all times.
• Because turnaround space is limited, designate and keep clear a specific area where emergency vehicles can turn around or reposition without obstruction.
• Keep at least one of the parking areas available and unblocked so arriving emergency vehicles have a staging area close to the residence.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway and walkway edges so responders moving on foot can see the full path ahead and avoid hazards at the sides.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the clusters nearest to the structure to increase open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees close to the structure to reduce the path fire can travel upward into the canopy.
• Trim shrubs and vegetation that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Cut grass around the structure and near tree clusters short, especially during dry periods.
• Clear branches and low growth along the rear of the property to allow people and equipment to move through more easily.
• Keep a clear path along the driveway by trimming any tree branches that hang over or into the travel lane.
• Separate scattered trees from nearby shrubs or tall grass by removing the ground-level vegetation between them.
• Remove dead branches and plant material from within tree clusters near the structure.
• Keep the open green space areas free of debris piles, cut vegetation, or other loose plant material that could carry fire toward the structure.
